About me
ALI HAMZA
ALI HAMZA
Hello, I’m Ali Hamza.

I’m a student who designs brands and builds games, learning technology every day.

I’m a 20-year-old student of Information Technology Management at Riphah International College in Lahore, Pakistan. I also hold a Hifz-e-Quran certificate, and before ADP I completed ICS and Matric.

My design journey started with Canva. I have done freelance logo and e-commerce graphics, and I run PixelCraft Digital for social posts, presentations and MS Office work.

As AH Studios Official, I independently build browser and Android games with HTML5 Canvas and JavaScript, using AI coding tools as assistants.

My interest in cyber security is growing through my university coursework on vulnerabilities and memory management. My goal is to become a Cyber Security Engineer, and I keep building my skills through coursework, personal projects and independent learning.

Game development

AH Studios Official. I independently build games with HTML5, JavaScript, Canvas, Web Audio and Android packaging.

Neon Racer

2D cyberpunk endless racing game
Currently in Google Play closed testing (not publicly released)AI-assisted development

A 2D cyberpunk endless racing game developed under AH Studios Official. Race down a neon highway, shoot enemies, dodge traffic and survive boss fights.

Links

Play live versionGitHub source code
Gameplay and mechanics
  • Steer between 3, 4 or 5 lanes (higher lane counts give higher score multipliers) with touch controls or optional tilt steering.
  • The car fires automatically. Destroy enemies, pick up coins and earn near-miss bonuses and combos.
  • Nitro boost and shield power-ups. In Classic mode, a traffic collision costs health instead of ending the run.
  • Boss fights appear at score milestones, with a larger mega boss every tenth boss.
  • Modes: Classic, Time Trial (survive 30 seconds), Elimination (one hit ends the run, double score) and Drift (no shooting, points for steering).
Main features
  • Six road environments: Highway, City, Desert, Forest, Night and Void, plus weather changes.
  • Eight car skins unlocked by reaching score targets, and eight upgrades bought with coins.
  • 48 achievements, daily challenges and a seven-day login reward.
  • Settings for steering sensitivity, music and sound volume, tilt steering and a replayable tutorial.
  • Automatic pause when the app goes to the background.
Visual design

A neon cyberpunk look: glowing cyan and magenta lane edges on a dark navy road, with outlined vehicles and effects. All visuals are drawn with Canvas shapes, with no external image assets.

Development process

I built the game as a single index.html file using HTML5 Canvas and vanilla JavaScript. Sound effects and music are generated in the browser with the Web Audio API, and progress is saved with LocalStorage. I wrap the web build with Capacitor to produce the Android app, and I test it on a real Android phone.

I fixed bugs along the way, such as bonus-score calculation, the speed cap and collision damage. The web version is hosted on GitHub Pages and works as an installable web app, with Google Analytics 4 added.

I used AI coding tools as assistants. I direct the design, test, debug and publish the game myself.

Technologies

HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Canvas API, Web Audio API, Capacitor, Android Studio.

Water Sort Puzzle

Color sorting puzzle game
Google Play release in preparationAI-assisted development

A color-sorting puzzle game with 9999 generated levels, developed under AH Studios Official. Pour liquids between tubes until each tube holds a single color.

Links

Play live versionGitHub source code
Gameplay
  • Tap a tube to select it, then tap another tube to pour the liquid.
  • Sort the colors so that each tube holds only one color.
  • Use undo and reset, spend coins on hints or an extra tube, and play the daily challenge once a day to build a streak.
Main features
  • 9999 generated levels.
  • Undo, hints and an extra-tube option.
  • A coin economy: coins are earned on the first clear of a level and spent on hints, tubes and the shop.
  • Daily challenge with a streak and bonus coins.
  • Shop with four backgrounds (Midnight, Sunset, Matrix, Ocean) and four tube skins (Glass, Neon, Wood, Crystal).
  • Achievements, saved progress and separate music and sound controls.
Level generation

Levels are generated by starting from a solved board and applying random reverse pours, so every level can be solved. Difficulty rises as levels increase: a new color is added every few levels and an extra empty tube appears later on. The daily challenge uses a date-based seed so it is the same for everyone on a given day.

UI and UX design

A dark gradient interface with large rounded buttons that are easy to tap on a phone. Liquid surfaces have a gentle wave, pours have squash-and-stretch motion, and haptic feedback is used on supported devices.

Development process

Like Neon Racer, it is a single index.html using HTML5 Canvas and vanilla JavaScript, with Web Audio API sounds and LocalStorage saves. I package it for Android with Capacitor. I used AI coding tools as assistants and handle the design, testing and publishing myself.

Technologies

HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Canvas API, Web Audio API, Capacitor, Android Studio.

Both games were developed with AI-assisted coding tools. I handle their design, testing and publishing. Neon Racer is in closed testing on Google Play, and Water Sort Puzzle is not yet released there.

Cyber security

Learning. Practicing. Understanding. Securing.

Cyber security is my long-term career direction. My current university coursework covers vulnerability research, memory management, software exploitation concepts and vulnerability mitigation. Everything here is studied material. I am not a penetration tester or a certified security professional, and I label coursework clearly.

A. Vulnerability research and CVE analysis

University cyber security courseworkVulnerability case study

CVE-2018-11529: VLC Media Player use-after-free

A study of a publicly documented vulnerability for my coursework. I did not discover or exploit it. I checked the details below against public records on 18 November 2026.

CVE IDCVE-2018-11529
ProductVideoLAN VLC media player
WeaknessCWE-416, Use After Free
Published (NVD)11 July 2018
Affected versionsNVD: VLC 2.2.x, listed up to and including 2.2.8
Severity (NVD)CVSS v3.0 base score 8.0, High (CVSS v2.0: 6.8, Medium)
CVSS v3.0 vectorAV:A / AC:L / PR:N / UI:R / S:U / C:H / I:H / A:H
Fix reported by Debianvlc 3.0.3-1-0+deb9u1 in DSA-4251-1
1. Vulnerability overview

NVD and MITRE describe VLC media player 2.2.x as prone to a use-after-free vulnerability that an attacker could use to execute arbitrary code through crafted MKV files. Failed attempts would likely end in a crash (denial of service).

Source difference: Debian’s advisory DSA-4251-1 for the same CVE describes the fixed bug as a use-after-free in VLC’s MP4 demuxer. The sources disagree on the affected component, so I treat the exact component as unresolved. My assignment follows the NVD description (MKV).

2. Root cause

A use-after-free happens when a program frees a block of memory but keeps a pointer to it, and later uses that pointer. The root cause is a mistake in how the media parser manages the lifetime of an object while it handles a malformed file. I am describing the general weakness here and have not reviewed VLC’s source code.

3. Technical explanation (concepts)

Heap memory is allocated and released while a program runs. After a block is freed, the allocator can hand the same memory to something else. If an old, dangling pointer is then used, the program may read or write data it no longer owns. With crafted input, that can change program behavior. This is why my coursework connects use-after-free to heap management, object lifetime and dangling pointers.

4. Potential impact

NVD describes possible arbitrary code execution, with a crash as the likely result of a failed attempt. The CVSS vector shows that the user must open the file (UI:R), and rates confidentiality, integrity and availability impact as High.

5. Severity assessment

NVD lists a CVSS v3.0 base score of 8.0 (High) and a CVSS v2.0 score of 6.8 (Medium). Ubuntu rates its own priority for this CVE as Medium. Different organizations can weigh the same flaw differently, which is a useful lesson in itself.

6. Mitigation
  • Update VLC to a current 3.x release. Debian fixed the issue in vlc 3.0.3-1-0+deb9u1 (DSA-4251-1), and the Debian tracker references fixes in the VLC 3.0 branch.
  • Avoid opening media files from untrusted sources.
  • Keep the operating system and media players patched.
  • Vendor advisory: I could not verify a VideoLAN advisory for this CVE, and MITRE lists no vendor solution.
7. Learning outcomes
  • How heap allocation, deallocation and dangling pointers lead to use-after-free bugs.
  • How to read a CVE record, CWE category and CVSS vector.
  • Why patching and updates matter, and why sources can disagree on details.
Sources: NVD recordDebian DSA-4251-1Debian security tracker

B. Memory management and memory corruption (studied concepts)

Stack memoryMemory used for function calls and local variables, organized last in, first out.
Heap memoryMemory a program requests while it runs, for data whose size or lifetime is not fixed.
Memory allocationReserving a block of heap memory for use.
Memory deallocationReturning a block to the system when it is no longer needed.
Dangling pointerA pointer that still refers to memory that has already been freed.
Use-after-freeUsing memory after it has been freed, which can cause crashes or unsafe behavior.
Memory addressesNumbers that identify where data is stored in memory.
Memory regionsAreas such as code, data, heap and stack, each with its own purpose and permissions.
PE file structureThe layout of Windows executables: headers and sections.
CPU registersVery small, very fast storage locations inside the processor.
RAX registerA 64-bit general-purpose register on x64 that commonly holds function return values.
x64 architectureThe 64-bit version of the x86 instruction set, with 16 general-purpose registers.

C. Software exploitation fundamentals (educational)

Buffer overflowWriting past the end of a memory buffer and overwriting nearby data.
Return-oriented programming (ROP)A technique that chains small pieces of existing code, studied to understand how defenses like non-executable memory are bypassed.
Shellcode fundamentalsSmall machine-code payloads, studied as a concept.
Stack pivotingRedirecting the stack pointer to a different memory area.
Memory analysisInspecting what a program holds in memory while it runs.
DebuggingStepping through a program to understand its behavior.
BreakpointsMarkers that pause execution at a chosen instruction.
Object lifetimeHow long an object stays valid between creation and destruction.
Virtual memoryAddress translation that gives each process its own isolated view of memory.

D. Vulnerability assessment

CVE researchLooking up publicly known vulnerabilities by their CVE identifier.
CVSS scoringA 0 to 10 scale for rating vulnerability severity.
Confidentiality, integrity, availabilityThe three security properties used to describe impact.
Risk assessmentWeighing how likely and how damaging a vulnerability is.
Mitigation and patchingReducing risk through updates, configuration and safer habits.
